web_title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
book_title: Chapter 2: Inside the Film Stack — Sun Control, Paint Protection & Specialty Industrial
question: What exact products generate GHFL's revenue and profits, and how does each segment work in the real world from factory extrusion to end-customer installation?

epigraph.quote: Value-added specialty manufacturing is won in micron-level tolerances—where a millimeter-thin polymer layer solves heat rejection, stone-chip impact, or high-speed packaging shrinkage.
epigraph.author: Polymer Engineering Maxim

web_blocks.title: 2.1 Segment Architecture: CPD vs. IPD and the 86–87% Value-Added Mix

web_blocks.html: Garware Hi-Tech Films reports across two main divisions [1, 10, 20]. The Consumer Product Division (CPD) sells Sun Control Films (SCF) and Paint Protection Films (PPF) [1, 10, 20]. The Industrial Product Division (IPD) makes high-shrink, lidding, release-liner, electrical insulation, and thermal lamination polyester films [1, 10, 20]. Across FY26 and H1 FY27, Value-Added Products (VAP) made up 86% to 87% of total revenue [4, 11]. Commodity BOPET films have been trimmed to roughly 13–14% [4, 11]. CPD drives about 68–70%+ of total business profits [10, 20]. Its revenue per ton of polymer is many times higher than in industrial packaging because products are sold by the square foot with multi-year warranties [10, 20].

web_blocks.title: 2.2 Concrete End-to-End Customer Examples Across All Three Segments

web_blocks.html: 1. Sun Control Films (SCF — Auto & Buildings): Picture an office tower builder in Dubai or a car owner in Phoenix, Arizona, fighting intense solar heat and UV rays. A Phoenix tint shop orders rolls of GHFL's Global Window Films nano-ceramic series [16]. In India, an authorized detailer installs Garware Ice Cool Shield SG 82 on a front windshield [16]. That film blocks high infrared heat while keeping 80%+ visible light transmission to meet road rules [16]. At Waluj, GHFL extrudes optical-grade PET film from its own chips, embeds IR-blocking nano-ceramic particles, and adds adhesive and a hard coat [15, 16]. In India, full-car Ice Cool packages retail at ₹15,000–₹22,000+ GST (material cost ~₹145/sq. ft.). In the US, pro installs fetch $300–$800, leaving healthy margins for GHFL and its installers.

2. Paint Protection Films (PPF — Car Surface Armor): Consider a buyer taking delivery of a ₹75 lakh SUV in Bengaluru or a sports sedan in Texas. They want protection from highway gravel chips, swirl marks, and bird-dropping stains. The buyer visits one of 250+ Garware Application Studios (GAS) and picks Garware Titanium PPF (8-mil TPU with a self-healing topcoat) or Garware Matte PPF [4, 15]. Before now, GHFL imported raw TPU film, added adhesive and topcoat in-house, and sold wholesale rolls at ~₹65,000–₹75,000 in India. Full-body studio wraps bill at ₹50,000–₹1,20,000+ in India and $2,000–$4,000 in the US. With its 360 LSF TPU line opening in Q3 FY27 alongside Lubrizol, GHFL now brings core TPU extrusion in-house [5, 11].

3. Industrial Product Division (IPD — High-Shrink & Release Liners): Think of a global drink bottler in Europe or India launching a curved PET bottle that needs a full 360-degree printed sleeve. Standard film wrinkles on tight curves. Instead, the printer buys GHFL's high-shrink polyester film made at its 42,000 MT IPD plant with exact shrinkage control [4, 17]. Tape and medical-patch makers also buy GHFL's silicone-coated release liners, while electronics plants buy insulation PET grades. Though lower-margin than PPF, these IPD lines keep the 66,000 MT chips plant running at high base loads. That spreads fixed plant costs across the entire Waluj–Chikalthana site [4, 15].

web_blocks.title: Next-Horizon Specialty: PDLC Smart Architecture Films
paragraphs: Beyond conventional tinted glazing, GHFL is commercializing Polymer-Dispersed Liquid Crystal (PDLC) switchable privacy films for commercial conference rooms, hospitals, and luxury automotive sunroofs—allowing glass to toggle electronically from transparent to opaque on demand [11].

web_blocks.title: 2.3 Product Portfolio Depth: From Entry-Level Protect to Matte & Colored PPF

web_blocks.html: Within PPF alone, GHFL offers tiered SKUs for every price point [4, 10]. Entry-level Garware Protect and Plus rolls sell at ₹36,000–₹50,000 wholesale per roll [4, 10]. Flagship Garware Titanium and Matte rolls sell at ₹65,000–₹75,000 wholesale, alongside colored and fashion PPF wraps [4, 10]. In Sun Control Films, the range covers dyed auto films, sputtered metallic building films, safety glazing films, and clear IR-blocking windshield films like Ice Cool Shield [15, 16]. This wide catalog lets dealers in 90+ countries source their entire film stack from one integrated supplier.

book_paragraphs: Once you know how Garware got here, the next question is simple: what actually leaves the factory gates in Aurangabad, and who writes the checks? In financial filings, the company splits into two divisions—the Consumer Product Division, or CPD, and the Industrial Product Division, or IPD. In practice, you and I should think of the business as three distinct product engines that together keep 86% to 87% of revenue inside high-value specialty films, leaving only 13% to 14% in commodity polyester.

The largest engine, generating roughly 51% of FY26 revenue, is Sun Control Films. Imagine an automotive tint shop in Phoenix or a commercial glazing contractor in Dubai trying to keep a building's cooling load down without turning the glass into a dark mirror. In India, where dark tints on car windows remain restricted, a driver taking delivery of a new SUV visits an authorized detailing studio and asks for Garware Ice Cool Shield on the front windshield. That film looks virtually clear—letting over 80% of visible light through—yet blocks infrared heat and ultraviolet rays using nano-ceramic dispersions embedded inside the polyester layers. A full-car package in India retails around ₹15,000 to ₹22,000, while U.S. installers using Garware's Global Window Films brand bill $300 to $800 per vehicle.

The fastest-growing engine, at roughly 24% of FY26 revenue, is Paint Protection Film, or PPF. Unlike polyester window tint, PPF is an 8-mil thick thermoplastic polyurethane armor applied over a car's painted body panels. When gravel hits the hood on a highway or a car wash leaves swirl marks, the elastomeric topcoat literally heals itself with ambient heat from the sun or warm water. A luxury car owner in Mumbai or Texas brings their vehicle to one of over 250 Garware Application Studios for a full-body wrap—Garware Protect, Titanium, or Matte—paying ₹50,000 to ₹1,20,000 in India or $2,000 to $4,000 in North America. Because PPF commands far higher revenue per square foot than window tint, scaling it from 300 to 600 lakh square feet—and backward-integrating into TPU extrusion with Lubrizol—has been the primary driver behind Garware's margin expansion.

Finally, the Industrial Product Division accounts for the remaining 25% of revenue. Here, Garware supplies high-shrink polyester films for contoured beverage bottle sleeves, silicone release liners for tapes and medical patches, thermal lamination films, and electrical insulation films. These industrial grades carry lower margins than PPF, so why keep them? Because they absorb baseload capacity at the 66,000-ton polyester chips plant. Without IPD keeping the upstream polymerization reactors humming, the unit cost of every square foot of specialty window film would climb. Together, CPD's brand pull and IPD's baseload scale form a self-reinforcing manufacturing stack.

book_subsections.title: From Kilograms to Square Feet: Why Product Mix Drives Margin Power
paragraphs: There is a simple mental model that explains almost everything about Garware's profitability over the past decade: the shift from selling polymer by the kilogram to selling engineered optical and protective layers by the square foot. Commodity packaging film is priced per kilogram at a thin spread over PTA and MEG feedstock costs. By contrast, a square foot of nano-ceramic window film or self-healing TPU Paint Protection Film sells on thermal rejection, optical clarity, anti-yellowing durability, and multi-year warranty trust.

And Garware is not standing still at automotive PPF and window tint. Management is actively commercializing Polymer-Dispersed Liquid Crystal, or PDLC, switchable privacy films for commercial conference rooms, hospitals, and luxury vehicle sunroofs—allowing glass to flip from transparent to opaque at the touch of a switch. Each new functional layer added in Aurangabad widens the gap between Garware's realization per ton and that of standard packaging peers.

Equally important is how Garware tiers its product ladder within each vertical. In Paint Protection Film, an entry-level detailing shop can stock Garware Protect or Plus rolls at ₹36,000 to ₹50,000 per roll for budget-conscious buyers, while luxury studios install Garware Titanium or Matte PPF at ₹65,000 to ₹75,000 per roll alongside newer colored fashion PPF wraps. In Sun Control Films, the catalog spans everything from clear infrared-blocking windshield films like Ice Cool Shield to heavy-duty architectural safety and security glazing for commercial towers.

That tiered SKU architecture gives international distributors a compelling reason to consolidate orders with Garware rather than juggling four separate niche suppliers. When one vertically integrated plant can ship dyed tint, nano-ceramic solar film, self-healing TPU armor, and industrial shrink sleeves on the same bill of lading, both factory utilization and distributor stickiness rise together.

book_callouts.title: Follow the Square-Foot Economics
book_callouts.text: As GHFL shifts capacity from commodity BOPET (sold by the kilogram) to Sun Control Films and TPU Paint Protection Films (sold by the square foot), revenue and EBITDA per ton of polymer processed multiply dramatically.
